title: Job 33
paragraphs: ¹ "And now, Job, listen to my words; pay attention to everything I say. ² I have opened my mouth and the words are ready on my tongue. ³ My words come from an honest heart; my lips will speak only what I know to be true. ⁴ The spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty has given me life. ⁵ If you can, answer me. Take your stand before me and speak.

⁶ Look, before God I am just as you are; I too was formed from clay. ⁷ You need not be frightened of me, and I will not come down hard on you. ⁸ But I have heard you speak with my own ears — I have heard the very words: ⁹ 'I am pure and without sin; I am innocent; there is no guilt in me. ¹⁰ Yet God has found fault with me; he treats me as his enemy.

¹¹ He has put my feet in chains; he watches every path I take.' ¹² But I tell you — in this you are not right. I will answer you: God is greater than any human being. ¹³ Why do you quarrel with him? He does not owe an account of all his actions. ¹⁴ For God speaks in one way, then another, and people do not always notice. ¹⁵ He speaks in dreams and visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, while they slumber in their beds.

¹⁶ Then he opens their ears and fills them with instruction, ¹⁷ turning them away from wrong and keeping pride at bay, ¹⁸ holding the soul back from the pit and keeping life from the sword. ¹⁹ Or a person may be chastened by suffering in bed, with constant pain in every bone, ²⁰ so that even food becomes revolting and every delicacy is loathsome.

²¹ His flesh wastes away until it cannot be seen, and his bones stand out, bare. ²² His soul draws close to the pit; his life to the agents of death. ²³ But if there is an angel at his side, one messenger among a thousand, to reveal to him what is right, ²⁴ then God shows mercy and says, 'Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom.' ²⁵ His flesh becomes fresher than a child's; he returns to the days of his youth.

²⁶ He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God's face and shouts for joy, and God restores him to full standing. ²⁷ He goes before others and says, 'I sinned and twisted what was right, yet it did not profit me.' ²⁸ God has delivered him from going down into the pit, and he will see the light of life. ²⁹ Yes, God does all this — twice, even three times — with a person, ³⁰ to pull their soul back from the pit and let them live in the light.

³¹ "Pay attention, Job — listen to me; stay quiet, and I will speak. ³² If you have anything to say, then answer me; speak up, for I would love to see you vindicated. ³³ But if not, then listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom."
